existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Direct cost of reprogramming to separate disclosable data
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge the requester the agency's direct cost of reprogramming a computer system where reprogramming is required to separate disclosable from nondisclosable information stored electronically.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Disclosable info is on a computer/analogous system AND reprogramming is required to segregate it
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A public agency may charge a person who makes a request for disclosable information the agency's direct cost of reprogramming a computer system if: (1) the disclosable information is stored on a computer tape, computer disc, or a similar or analogous record system; and (2) the public agency is required to reprogram the computer system to separate the disclosable information from nondisclosable information.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Charge capped at 'direct cost' (ceiling). Attaches to the segregability duty in IN-0011.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Copying fee ceiling (greater of per-page rate or actual cost)
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of ten cents ($0.10) per non-color page or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per color page, or the agency's actual cost.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of: (1) ten cents ($0.10) per page for copies that are not color copies or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for color copies; or (2) the actual cost to the agency.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling. For local agencies the copying fee schedule is established by the fiscal body (see IN-0019). Same concept as a fixed-25-cent rule elsewhere per constraint-basis guidance.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge a fee for providing an electronic map based upon a reasonable percentage of the agency's direct cost of maintaining, upgrading, and enhancing the electronic map.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Request is for an electronic map
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A public agency may charge a fee, uniform to all purchasers, for providing an electronic map that is based upon a reasonable percentage of the agency's direct cost of maintaining, upgrading, and enhancing the electronic map.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Special record type (electronic map) with a distinct fee basis; ceiling tied to a reasonable percentage of direct cost.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge any reasonable fee agreed on in an enhanced-access contract under section 3.5 for providing enhanced access to public records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Access is provided via an enhanced-access contract under § 5-14-3-3.5
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A public agency may charge any reasonable fee agreed on in the contract under section 3.5 of this chapter for providing enhanced access to public records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: 'Reasonable fee agreed on in the contract' - no statutory number; soft-standard, contract-set.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Copying fee schedule set by fiscal body
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For a local public agency, the fiscal body of the political subdivision establishes the copying fee schedule by ordinance, and the fee must be uniform.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The fiscal body (as defined in IC 36-1-2-6) of the political subdivision shall establish a fee schedule for the certification or copying of documents ... The fee for copying documents may not exceed [the statutory ceiling].
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Structural: the operative-value ceiling lives in IN-0015; this row is the requirement that a local fiscal body (not the records custodian) set the schedule. Paraphrase - exact subsection text not captured verbatim; verify subsection lettering and the uniformity clause.
